sents.t: On the second Sunday in May, Americans celebrate Mother’s Day.
My mother lives on the other side of the world, so I couldn’t visit her.
Instead, I ordered flowers online from a shop in her city.
On Sunday morning, I made a video call.
She was holding the flowers, and she had happy tears in her eyes.
“I’ve missed you so much, Sam,” she said.
“You’ve been in America for almost a year!”
“I know, Mom. I’ve learned so much since I arrived, and I’ve made good friends here.” Max barked at the screen.
Rosa has been like a mother to me since my first day in Oakville.
So Lily and I made brunch for her: pancakes, fresh strawberries, and coffee.
Danny, Sarah, Mia, and Leo came too.
Mia gave Rosa a handmade card with a drawing of Max.
My mom wanted to meet Rosa, so I called her again.
They couldn’t speak the same language, but they smiled and waved at each other.
“Your son is a wonderful young man,” Rosa said.
I translated, and my mom cried again.
